records.verificationNote: Read CDL pp.7-8, 94-97. Judgment on Code I: CDL General Provision 2 (p.4) requires authorization for starred entries unless used under the CDL-specified conditions. This record treats the controlled-substance policy limits as those conditions. If Medi-Cal Rx reads starred entries as PA-required, every opioid row here moves to paRequired. Meperidine elixir requires a PA (p.94) but is outside this class. Hydrocodone/APAP chosen as a usual short-acting generic (judgment). [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: CDL p.4 General Provision 2: "Code I drugs marked with a symbol (*) require authorization in accordance with Section 51003 unless used under the conditions specified in the Contract Drugs List". For zolpidem (p.126) and hydrocodone/APAP (p.94) the printed Code I condition is "Refer to the Controlled Substance Policy section for drug-specific limitations" (p.7), so the star is a use limit, not a PA; contrast meperidine elixir, which prints "requires a PA" (p.94). Pick kept; verification stays partial (starred wording is ambiguous on its face). Unlisted-product rows quote p.4: "Legend drugs not listed may be covered subject to authorization from a Medi-Cal consultant." Confirmed by text search of the full CDL: none of eszopiclone, zaleplon, tapentadol appear.]

records.verificationNote: Preferred: hydrocodone/acetaminophen tabs 5-325 mg (PDF p.45, Tier 1, no flag); opioid rows PDF pp.44-47. Controlled substance. No quantity or day-supply limit is printed on the preferred row, so none is recorded. Printed opioid IR: hydrocodone/APAP, oxycodone IR, oxycodone/APAP, tramadol and tramadol/APAP, APAP/codeine, hydromorphone tabs, morphine IR tabs (Tier 2, PDF p.47). Tapentadol (Nucynta) is not printed; treated as unconfirmed. Methadone tabs are printed (PDF p.46) but outside the IR class list. Document says: "Kaiser Foundation Health Plan does not have a requirement for PA" (PDF p.6) and "does not have a requirement for Step Therapy" (PDF p.7).
